description: Six sequencers in one module, each drawing a voltage sequence and a gate sequence of up to 32 steps, with its own length, clock and pair of outputs

params.text: Sets how many steps that sequencer plays before returning to its first, 1 to 32
Selects that sequencer for editing, so the display draws its voltage and gate steps

inputs.text: A rising edge advances every sequencer that has no cable in its own step input
A rising edge returns every sequencer to its first step, and clock pulses are ignored for the following 1ms
A rising edge advances that sequencer alone, in place of the common STEP input

outputs.text: The voltage drawn at the current step of that sequencer, in the range chosen for it
A 10ms 10V trigger on every step marked in the gate sequence of that sequencer

notes: drag in the upper half of the display to draw voltages and in the lower half to set gates
Quick Key Reference in the right-click menu lists the keys the display responds to, among them f to freeze the sequencers for editing and r to randomise the sequence under the pointer
every step of every sequence starts at zero, so the voltage outputs stay at the bottom of their range and no gate is put out until the display is drawn on
menu: Sequencer Settings — All Sequencers, and Sequencer #1 through Sequencer #6, each holding that sequencer's Output Range, Snap and Sample & Hold
Snap — None, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 32 or 36, rounding drawn voltages to that many steps; reached through Sequencer Settings
Sample & Hold — Off or On, holding the voltage output between gates instead of changing it every step; reached through Sequencer Settings
Reset Mode — two choices printed Next clock input. and Instant, setting whether a reset takes effect on the next clock or at once
Output Range — the span of a sequencer's voltage output, from -10.0 to 10.0 down to 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 to 10.0 to start with; reached through Sequencer Settings
Quick Key Reference — lists the keys the display responds to while the pointer is over the module
